PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: Not applicable (fetal sample)
Sample Type: Fetal tissue
Sample ID: [redacted ID]
Referring Clinician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal genetic testing of fetal tissue following detection of fetal abnormalities. Suspected chromosomal abnormalities or genetic disorders related to fetal development.

TEST PERFORMED
Oligonucleotide Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH)
- Platform: GeneScan 4500
- Array design: ~60,000 genome-wide oligonucleotide probes
- Median resolution: 120kb
- Analysis software: GenomeView
- Reference genome: GRCh37/hg19

Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
- Assessment for triploidy

RESULTS

ARRAY CGH ANALYSIS
Result: arr(1-22,X)x2
Interpretation: Normal female chromosome complement

No copy number imbalances detected.
- Chromosomes 1-22: Normal copy number (x2)
- Chromosome X: Normal copy number (x2)
- Chromosome Y: Not detected (consistent with female)

QF-PCR ANALYSIS
Result: No evidence of triploidy
All markers showed normal diallelic patterns consistent with diploid female karyotype.

TECHNICAL SUMMARY
- DNA quality: Satisfactory
- Array quality metrics: Pass
- Call rate: >99%
- Derivative log ratio spread (DLRS): 0.18

INTERPRETATION
This analysis shows a normal female chromosome complement with no detectable chromosomal abnormalities. No imbalances greater than 1Mb were identified. No smaller imbalances of known pathogenicity or relevance to fetal abnormalities were detected.

The normal array CGH result indicates that no detectable chromosomal abnormalities could explain the fetal abnormalities observed on ultrasound.

LIMITATIONS
This test cannot detect:
- Balanced chromosomal rearrangements (translocations, inversions)
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%)
- Point mutations or small insertions/deletions
- Methylation abnormalities or uniparental disomy
- Polyploidy other than triploidy

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis is indicated for this sample based on these results. If clinical suspicion remains high, consideration may be given to:
- Targeted gene sequencing if specific genetic syndrome suspected
- Parental karyotyping if balanced rearrangement suspected
- Clinical genetics consultation for further evaluation

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
